items.q: A register stores 8 bits. How many hexadecimal digits are needed to write its whole content?
items.s: One hex digit covers four bits, so 8 bits need 8/4 = 2 digits.

items.q: How many octal digits are needed to express every value that fits in 12 bits?
items.s: One octal digit covers three bits, so 12 bits need 12/3 = 4 digits.

items.q: How many binary places are required to express the decimal number 3079?
items.s: The largest power of two below 3079 is 2^11, so 12 bits are needed.

items.q: A complete truth table is required for a circuit with 6 inputs. How many rows must it contain?
items.s: Every input doubles the rows, so 2^6 = 64 rows.

items.q: A multiplexer is controlled by 1 select lines. How many data inputs can it choose between?
items.s: Each select line doubles the choices, so 2^1 = 2 inputs.

items.q: A combinational path passes through 7 gate levels and each gate delays by 10 ns. What is the worst case path delay?
items.s: Delays in series add, so 7 x 10 = 70 ns.

items.q: A counting circuit must pass through 10 distinct states. What is the smallest number of flip flops that will serve?
items.s: k stages give 2^k states, so the least k with 2^k at least 10 is 4.

items.q: A memory contains 8192 addressable words. How many address lines must the chip be given?
items.s: The address must count up to 8192, so k address lines give 2^k words and 2^13 = 8192.

items.q: A gate can sink 20 mA at its output, and every input it drives sinks 1 mA when low. What is the fan out allowed by current sinking?
items.s: Fan out = sink capability divided by current per input = 20/1 = 20 inputs.

items.q: An 8 bit word holds the value 15. How many of its bits are set to one?
items.s: 15 in binary is 00001111, which has 4 ones.

items.q: A seven segment display shows the decimal digit 6. How many of its segments are lit?
items.s: The digit 6 needs 6 of the seven segments.

items.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 6F6 to decimal.
items.s: Each hexadecimal place is a power of sixteen, and 6F6 works out to 1782.

items.q: A binary coded decimal word carries 5 decimal digits. How many bits does it contain?
items.s: Each decimal digit uses four bits, so 5 digits take 5 x 4 = 20 bits.

items.q: A nibble of a register holds the hexadecimal digit E. What decimal value does that nibble stand for?
items.s: The hex digit E has place value 14 in decimal.

items.q: How many minterms exist for a function of 6 variables?
items.s: There is one minterm per input pattern, so 2^6 = 64.

items.q: A Boolean function of 5 variables is written in canonical product of sums form. How many maxterms appear in the complete form?
items.s: There is one maxterm per input pattern, so 2^5 = 32.

items.q: How many cells must a Karnaugh map have if it is to represent a function of 5 variables?
items.s: One cell per minterm gives 2^5 = 32 cells.

items.q: A group of 8 adjacent cells is circled on a Karnaugh map. How many variables are eliminated from the corresponding term?
items.s: Grouping 8 = 2^3 cells removes 3 variables from the term.

items.q: A binary decoder is given 4 input lines. How many output lines does it have?
items.s: One output is active for each input code, so 2^4 = 16 outputs.

items.q: A ripple carry adder is built from half adders for the first stage and full adders afterwards to add two 8 bit words. How many adder blocks are needed in all?
items.s: One block serves each of the 8 columns: a half adder for the first column and a full adder for each of the remaining 7 columns, giving 8 blocks in all.

items.q: A half adder has 2 inputs listed in its full truth table including the carry in for comparison. How many rows does that table have?
items.s: With 2 inputs the table needs 2^2 = 4 rows.

items.q: The 12 bit two's complement word 111101100000 is to be read as a signed number. What decimal value does it represent?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative. Its value is 3936 minus 2^12 = -160.

items.q: A signed integer is stored in two's complement in 16 bits. What is the magnitude of the most negative value it can hold?
items.s: The most negative value is -2^15, whose magnitude is 32768.

items.q: A binary counter is built from 8 flip flops. What is its natural modulus?
items.s: The counter runs through 2^8 = 256 states before repeating.

items.q: A ripple counter has 4 stages and each flip flop has a propagation delay of 20 ns. What is the total delay before the output settles after a clock?
items.s: The delays of the 4 stages add up, so 4 x 20 = 80 ns.

items.q: A 10 bit word is to be shifted out of a shift register one place per clock. How many clock pulses are needed to clear the whole word?
items.s: Each of the 10 bits needs one clock pulse, so 10 pulses empty the register.

items.q: A ring counter is built from 10 flip flops. How many distinct states does it pass through?
items.s: A single one circulates through the 10 stages, so the counter has 10 states.

items.q: A Johnson counter is built from 9 flip flops. How many distinct states does it pass through?
items.s: Inverting feedback doubles the number of stages, so the counter has 2 x 9 = 18 states.

items.q: A memory is organised as 128 words of 4 bits. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 128 x 4 = 512 bits.

items.q: A store of 4096 words is to be built from chips each holding 256 words. How many chips are required?
A read only memory is used to store a function of 4 inputs, one word per input pattern. How many words must the memory hold?
items.s: Each of the 2^4 = 16 input patterns needs its own word.

items.q: A logic family guarantees a minimum output high of 3 V and requires at least 2.2 V at its inputs. What is the high level noise margin in volts?
items.s: Noise margin = output high minus input high = 3 - 2.2 = 0.8 V.

items.q: A synchronous circuit has a critical path of 20 ns between registers. What is the highest clock frequency it can use, in MHz?
items.s: Frequency = 1/period = 1/20 ns = 50 MHz.

items.q: A gate has a propagation delay of 15 ns and dissipates 5 mW. What is its delay power product in picojoules?
items.s: Delay power product = 15 ns x 5 mW = 75 pJ.

items.q: An integrated circuit contains 20 gates, each dissipating 10 mW. What is the total dissipation in milliwatts?
items.s: Total = 20 x 10 = 200 mW.

items.q: A 12 bit analogue to digital converter has a full scale range of 10 V. What is its resolution in volts?
items.s: Resolution = full scale / 2^bits = 10/4096 = 0.0024 V.

items.q: An 5 bit digital to analogue converter has a full scale output of 5 V. What output results from the input code 2?
items.s: Output = full scale x code/2^bits = 5 x 2/32 = 0.3125 V.

items.q: The integer 200 is shifted left by 1 places inside a register that is wide enough to hold the result. What value does the register then hold?
items.s: A left shift of 1 multiplies by 2^1, so 200 x 2 = 400.

items.q: Two 8 bit words 01100111 and 11000010 are combined with a bitwise AND. What decimal value results?
items.s: A bit is one only where both words have a one, and that pattern is worth 66.

items.q: Two 8 bit words 51 and 147 are combined with a bitwise OR. What decimal value results?
items.s: Bringing together the set bits of both words gives 179.

items.q: Two 8 bit words 59 and 171 are combined with an exclusive OR. What decimal value results?
items.s: Only the positions where the words differ survive, and they are worth 144.

items.q: Convert the binary number 1001000 to decimal.
items.s: Adding the place values 1, 2, 4, 8 ... where a one appears in 1001000 gives 72.

items.q: A register stores 20 bits. How many hexadecimal digits are needed to write its whole content?
items.s: One hex digit covers four bits, so 20 bits need 20/4 = 5 digits.

items.q: How many binary places are required to express the decimal number 659?
items.s: The largest power of two below 659 is 2^9, so 10 bits are needed.

items.q: A complete truth table is required for a circuit with 5 inputs. How many rows must it contain?
items.s: Every input doubles the rows, so 2^5 = 32 rows.

items.q: A multiplexer is controlled by 3 select lines. How many data inputs can it choose between?
items.s: Each select line doubles the choices, so 2^3 = 8 inputs.

items.q: A combinational path passes through 4 gate levels and each gate delays by 12 ns. What is the worst case path delay?
items.s: Delays in series add, so 4 x 12 = 48 ns.

items.q: A counting circuit must pass through 16 distinct states. What is the smallest number of flip flops that will serve?
items.s: k stages give 2^k states, so the least k with 2^k at least 16 is 4.

items.q: A memory contains 2048 addressable words. How many address lines must the chip be given?
items.s: The address must count up to 2048, so k address lines give 2^k words and 2^11 = 2048.

items.q: A gate can sink 8 mA at its output, and every input it drives sinks 0.5 mA when low. What is the fan out allowed by current sinking?
items.s: Fan out = sink capability divided by current per input = 8/0.5 = 16 inputs.

items.q: An 8 bit word holds the value 452. How many of its bits are set to one?
items.s: 452 in binary is 111000100, which has 4 ones.

items.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 5C8 to decimal.
items.s: Each hexadecimal place is a power of sixteen, and 5C8 works out to 1480.

items.q: A binary coded decimal word carries 3 decimal digits. How many bits does it contain?
items.s: Each decimal digit uses four bits, so 3 digits take 3 x 4 = 12 bits.

items.q: A nibble of a register holds the hexadecimal digit 3. What decimal value does that nibble stand for?
items.s: The hex digit 3 has place value 3 in decimal.

items.q: How many minterms exist for a function of 5 variables?
items.s: There is one minterm per input pattern, so 2^5 = 32.

items.q: A Boolean function of 4 variables is written in canonical product of sums form. How many maxterms appear in the complete form?
items.s: There is one maxterm per input pattern, so 2^4 = 16.

items.q: How many cells must a Karnaugh map have if it is to represent a function of 4 variables?
items.s: One cell per minterm gives 2^4 = 16 cells.

items.q: A group of 4 adjacent cells is circled on a Karnaugh map. How many variables are eliminated from the corresponding term?
items.s: Grouping 4 = 2^2 cells removes 2 variables from the term.

items.q: A binary decoder is given 3 input lines. How many output lines does it have?
items.s: One output is active for each input code, so 2^3 = 8 outputs.

items.q: The 12 bit two's complement word 100011111100 is to be read as a signed number. What decimal value does it represent?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative. Its value is 2300 minus 2^12 = -1796.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Digital to analogue converter?
o: a circuit that turns a binary word into a proportional voltage
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus
one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted
items.s: Digital to analogue converter: a circuit that turns a binary word into a proportional voltage. The other options describe Literal, Tri state output, Propagation delay product.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Universal gate.
o: the interval before the clock edge during which data must already be steady
the coding of each decimal digit separately as four binary places
a device from which any other logic function can be constructed
an output that can pull low but needs an external resistor to pull high
items.s: Universal gate: a device from which any other logic function can be constructed. The other options describe Setup time, Binary coded decimal, Open collector output.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Race condition?
o: a counting circuit that can be loaded with a chosen starting value
a fault in which the result depends on which of two nearly simultaneous changes arrives first
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
a reset input that acts at once without waiting for a clock edge
items.s: Race condition: a fault in which the result depends on which of two nearly simultaneous changes arrives first. The other options describe De Morgan law, Asynchronous clear, Presettable counter.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Transistor transistor logic?
o: a family built from bipolar transistors in which inputs are emitters
the voltage by which a level may be disturbed before it is misread
the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady
a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
items.s: Transistor transistor logic: a family built from bipolar transistors in which inputs are emitters. The other options describe Hold time, Truth table, Noise margin.

items.q: Quantisation error may be defined as
o: a device whose output is high only when every input is low
a signed notation in which a negative number is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
the difference between the true value and the nearest step a converter can represent
the identity by which a term swallows any larger term that contains it
items.s: Quantisation error: the difference between the true value and the nearest step a converter can represent. The other options describe Absorption rule, NOR gate, Two’s complement.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Two’s complement?
o: an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs
an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition
a memory whose content is lost when the supply is removed
a signed notation in which a negative number is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
items.s: Two’s complement: a signed notation in which a negative number is the inverse of its magnitude plus one. The other options describe Sum of products form, Don’t care condition, Volatile store.

items.q: All of the following belong to Data conversion and arithmetic circuits EXCEPT
o: Digital to analogue converter
Resolution of a converter
Clock skew
Analogue to digital converter
items.s: Every other option belongs to Data conversion and arithmetic circuits. “Clock skew” belongs to Sequential logic and flip flops, not Data conversion and arithmetic circuits.

items.q: Which term is described by “a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it”?
o: Counter
Ripple counter
Synchronous counter
Modulus
items.s: Ripple counter is a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines De Morgan law.
o: a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
the power of the base attached to each place in a positional numeral
an extra bit added so that the count of ones in a word is always even or always odd
items.s: De Morgan law: the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions. The other options describe Truth table, Bit position weight, Parity bit.

items.q: Hold time may be defined as
o: the number of distinct states that a counting circuit passes through
a circuit that forms the sum and carry of two single bits
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady
items.s: Hold time: the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady. The other options describe Modulus, Half adder, Propagation delay product.

items.q: The statement “a circuit that forms the sum and carry of two single bits” describes which of the following?
o: Exclusive OR
Combinational circuit
NAND gate
Half adder
items.s: Half adder is a circuit that forms the sum and carry of two single bits.

items.q: Which term is described by “a counting circuit that can be loaded with a chosen starting value”?
o: Asynchronous clear
Presettable counter
Counter
Shift register
items.s: Presettable counter is a counting circuit that can be loaded with a chosen starting value.

items.q: Which term is described by “a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input”?
o: Flip flop
State table
Latch
Race condition
items.s: State table is a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input.

items.q: Propagation delay product may be defined as
o: a counting circuit in which every stage receives the same clock at the same instant
the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
a device from which any other logic function can be constructed
items.s: Propagation delay product: the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation. The other options describe Synchronous counter, Universal gate, Hold time.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Full scale range?
o: the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent
a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock
a storage element that changes state whenever its enable input is active
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
items.s: Full scale range: the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent. The other options describe Shift register, Latch, De Morgan law.

items.q: Which term is described by “the number of inputs that one output can drive while keeping its levels valid”?
o: Tri state output
Fan out
Noise margin
Propagation delay product
items.s: Fan out is the number of inputs that one output can drive while keeping its levels valid.

items.q: Which term is described by “the interval before the clock edge during which data must already be steady”?
o: Setup time
State table
Race condition
Clock skew
items.s: Setup time is the interval before the clock edge during which data must already be steady.

items.q: Minterm may be defined as
o: the identity by which a term swallows any larger term that contains it
a product of every variable of a function that is true for exactly one input pattern
a device from which any other logic function can be constructed
a circuit that adds two bits together with a carry arriving from a lower place
items.s: Minterm: a product of every variable of a function that is true for exactly one input pattern. The other options describe Absorption rule, Full adder, Universal gate.

items.q: Shift register may be defined as
o: the difference between the high and the low output levels of a gate
a family built from bipolar transistors in which inputs are emitters
the number of distinct digit symbols used by a positional number system
a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock
items.s: Shift register: a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock. The other options describe Logic swing, Transistor transistor logic, Radix.

items.q: Least significant bit may be defined as
o: the rightmost digit of a binary word, which carries the smallest weight
the difference between the high and the low output levels of a gate
a symbol from zero to seven standing for three binary places
a group of storage elements that hold one binary word
items.s: Least significant bit: the rightmost digit of a binary word, which carries the smallest weight. The other options describe Register, Octal digit, Logic swing.

items.q: Flip flop may be defined as
o: a two state storage element that changes only at a defined edge of a clock
the power of the base attached to each place in a positional numeral
a conductor carrying one bit of the number that selects a stored word
a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it
items.s: Flip flop: a two state storage element that changes only at a defined edge of a clock. The other options describe Bit position weight, Address line, Ripple counter.

items.q: Chip select may be defined as
o: the input that enables a memory device to respond to the bus
the unsettled condition of a storage element that was clocked while its input was changing
a store that keeps its content without power and can be erased electrically in blocks
an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus
items.s: Chip select: the input that enables a memory device to respond to the bus. The other options describe Tri state output, Flash memory, Metastability.

items.q: The statement “a symbol from zero to nine or A to F standing for four binary places” describes which of the following?
o: Radix
Hexadecimal digit
Bit position weight
Octal digit
items.s: Hexadecimal digit is a symbol from zero to nine or A to F standing for four binary places.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Shift register?
o: a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock
the delay from presenting an address to receiving the word stored there
a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
a device whose output is high only when every input is low
items.s: Shift register: a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock. The other options describe Access time, NOR gate, Truth table.

items.q: All of the following belong to Counters and registers EXCEPT
o: Counter
Register
Shift register
Power dissipation
items.s: Every other option belongs to Counters and registers. “Power dissipation” belongs to Logic families and timing, not Counters and registers.

items.q: Which term is described by “an extra bit added so that the count of ones in a word is always even or always odd”?
o: Gray code
Binary coded decimal
Parity bit
Octal digit
items.s: Parity bit is an extra bit added so that the count of ones in a word is always even or always odd.

items.q: Which term is described by “the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent”?
o: Resolution of a converter
Full scale range
Successive approximation
Two’s complement
items.s: Full scale range is the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent.

items.q: Full scale range may be defined as
o: the internal conductor that selects every cell of one stored word
the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent
an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition
a symbol that takes only the value zero or one in base two
items.s: Full scale range: the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent. The other options describe Binary digit, Word line, Sum of products form.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Truth table?
o: a reset input that acts at once without waiting for a clock edge
an array whose stored content is fixed and can only be read
a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
a family built from bipolar transistors in which inputs are emitters
items.s: Truth table: a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs. The other options describe Transistor transistor logic, Read only memory, Asynchronous clear.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bit position weight.
o: a symbol from zero to seven standing for three binary places
the power of the base attached to each place in a positional numeral
the rightmost digit of a binary word, which carries the smallest weight
an ordering of binary words in which neighbours differ in exactly one place
items.s: Bit position weight: the power of the base attached to each place in a positional numeral. The other options describe Gray code, Octal digit, Least significant bit.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Clock skew?
o: a product of every variable of a function that is true for exactly one input pattern
a device whose output is low only when every input is high
the difference in arrival time of the clock at two different storage elements
the internal conductor that selects every cell of one stored word
items.s: Clock skew: the difference in arrival time of the clock at two different storage elements. The other options describe NAND gate, Minterm, Word line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Propagation delay?
o: one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted
the time between a change at an input and the resulting change at the output
the rightmost digit of a binary word, which carries the smallest weight
an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition
items.s: Propagation delay: the time between a change at an input and the resulting change at the output. The other options describe Literal, Least significant bit, Sum of products form.

items.q: Which term is described by “the leftmost digit of a binary word, which carries the greatest weight”?
o: Radix
Most significant bit
Bit position weight
Gray code
items.s: Most significant bit is the leftmost digit of a binary word, which carries the greatest weight.

items.q: Which term is described by “the voltage by which a level may be disturbed before it is misread”?
o: Noise margin
CMOS inverter
Fan out
Propagation delay product
items.s: Noise margin is the voltage by which a level may be disturbed before it is misread.

items.q: State table may be defined as
o: an arrangement of a function as sum terms multiplied together
a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input
a sum of every variable of a function that is false for exactly one input pattern
a store that keeps its content without power and can be erased electrically in blocks
items.s: State table: a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input. The other options describe Product of sums form, Flash memory, Maxterm.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Setup time?
o: an expression formed by adding together the minterms where the output is true
the time between a change at an input and the resulting change at the output
the interval before the clock edge during which data must already be steady
the coding of each decimal digit separately as four binary places
items.s: Setup time: the interval before the clock edge during which data must already be steady. The other options describe Propagation delay, Canonical sum, Binary coded decimal.

items.q: Which term is described by “an expression formed by adding together the minterms where the output is true”?
o: Canonical sum
Boolean variable
Karnaugh map
Minterm
items.s: Canonical sum is an expression formed by adding together the minterms where the output is true.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Counter.
o: the smallest change of input that a converter can distinguish
a circuit that steps through a fixed sequence of states on each clock
a circuit that freezes a changing voltage while it is being converted
a rectangular arrangement of cells in Gray order used to group minterms by eye
items.s: Counter: a circuit that steps through a fixed sequence of states on each clock. The other options describe Sample and hold, Resolution of a converter, Karnaugh map.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Minterm.
o: a symbol that takes only the value zero or one in base two
an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition
the coding of each decimal digit separately as four binary places
a product of every variable of a function that is true for exactly one input pattern
items.s: Minterm: a product of every variable of a function that is true for exactly one input pattern. The other options describe Binary digit, Binary coded decimal, Sum of products form.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines NOR gate.
o: a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
a device whose output is high only when every input is low
the input that enables a memory device to respond to the bus
the time between a change at an input and the resulting change at the output
items.s: NOR gate: a device whose output is high only when every input is low. The other options describe Propagation delay, Chip select, Truth table.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Analogue to digital converter.
o: a circuit that turns a measured voltage into a binary word
the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady
a conversion method that tests one bit at a time from the most significant downwards
a device from which any other logic function can be constructed
items.s: Analogue to digital converter: a circuit that turns a measured voltage into a binary word. The other options describe Universal gate, Successive approximation, Hold time.

items.q: Which term is described by “the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady”?
o: Metastability
Hold time
Clock skew
Propagation delay
items.s: Hold time is the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Product of sums form?
o: a quantity that can hold only the value true or the value false
an arrangement of a function as sum terms multiplied together
a circuit that turns a binary word into a proportional voltage
a rectangular arrangement of cells in Gray order used to group minterms by eye
items.s: Product of sums form: an arrangement of a function as sum terms multiplied together. The other options describe Digital to analogue converter, Boolean variable, Karnaugh map.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Analogue to digital converter?
o: a two input operation whose output is high when the inputs disagree
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
a circuit that turns a measured voltage into a binary word
a circuit that adds two bits together with a carry arriving from a lower place
items.s: Analogue to digital converter: a circuit that turns a measured voltage into a binary word. The other options describe Full adder, Exclusive OR, De Morgan law.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Propagation delay.
o: the time between a change at an input and the resulting change at the output
an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition
the smallest change of input that a converter can distinguish
a circuit that freezes a changing voltage while it is being converted
items.s: Propagation delay: the time between a change at an input and the resulting change at the output. The other options describe Sample and hold, Sum of products form, Resolution of a converter.

items.q: The statement “a group of storage elements that hold one binary word” describes which of the following?
o: Ring counter
Register
Shift register
Synchronous counter
items.s: Register is a group of storage elements that hold one binary word.

items.q: The statement “a memory whose content is lost when the supply is removed” describes which of the following?
o: Address line
Read only memory
Volatile store
Random access memory
items.s: Volatile store is a memory whose content is lost when the supply is removed.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that a term implied by two others may be deleted without changing a function”?
o: Consensus theorem
Boolean variable
Don’t care condition
De Morgan law
items.s: Consensus theorem is the rule that a term implied by two others may be deleted without changing a function.

items.q: Which term is described by “the unsettled condition of a storage element that was clocked while its input was changing”?
o: Metastability
Clock skew
Setup time
Flip flop
items.s: Metastability is the unsettled condition of a storage element that was clocked while its input was changing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Register.
o: a device whose output is low only when every input is high
a group of storage elements that hold one binary word
the interval before the clock edge during which data must already be steady
a device whose output is high only when every input is low
items.s: Register: a group of storage elements that hold one binary word. The other options describe NAND gate, NOR gate, Setup time.

items.q: Which term is described by “a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off”?
o: Logic swing
Power dissipation
CMOS inverter
Propagation delay product
items.s: CMOS inverter is a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off.

items.q: The statement “a shift register whose last stage feeds the first so that a single one circulates” describes which of the following?
o: Ripple counter
Ring counter
Synchronous counter
Johnson counter
items.s: Ring counter is a shift register whose last stage feeds the first so that a single one circulates.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Latch.
o: a symbol from zero to seven standing for three binary places
a conversion method that tests one bit at a time from the most significant downwards
the interval after the clock edge during which data must stay steady
a storage element that changes state whenever its enable input is active
items.s: Latch: a storage element that changes state whenever its enable input is active. The other options describe Successive approximation, Octal digit, Hold time.

items.q: All of the following belong to Boolean algebra and minimisation EXCEPT
o: Minterm
Half adder
Boolean variable
Literal
items.s: Every other option belongs to Boolean algebra and minimisation. “Half adder” belongs to Combinational logic, not Boolean algebra and minimisation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines CMOS inverter?
o: a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off
a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input
the condition in which a result is too large for the number of places available
items.s: CMOS inverter: a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off. The other options describe Overflow, Truth table, State table.

items.q: Successive approximation may be defined as
o: a conversion method that tests one bit at a time from the most significant downwards
the energy a gate converts to heat in each second of operation
a storage element that changes state whenever its enable input is active
an arrangement of a function as sum terms multiplied together
items.s: Successive approximation: a conversion method that tests one bit at a time from the most significant downwards. The other options describe Power dissipation, Latch, Product of sums form.

items.q: The statement “a circuit that adds two bits together with a carry arriving from a lower place” describes which of the following?
o: Half adder
Sum of products form
NOR gate
Full adder
items.s: Full adder is a circuit that adds two bits together with a carry arriving from a lower place.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Race condition.
o: a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off
a shift register whose last stage feeds the first so that a single one circulates
a fault in which the result depends on which of two nearly simultaneous changes arrives first
the difference in arrival time of the clock at two different storage elements
items.s: Race condition: a fault in which the result depends on which of two nearly simultaneous changes arrives first. The other options describe Ring counter, Clock skew, CMOS inverter.

items.q: Which term is described by “the input that enables a memory device to respond to the bus”?
o: Access time
Word line
Flash memory
Chip select
items.s: Chip select is the input that enables a memory device to respond to the bus.

items.q: Which term is described by “a memory whose content is lost when the supply is removed”?
o: Programmable array logic
Random access memory
Volatile store
Access time
items.s: Volatile store is a memory whose content is lost when the supply is removed.

items.q: Which of the following best describes NAND gate?
o: an output that can pull low but needs an external resistor to pull high
a device whose output is low only when every input is high
an extra bit added so that the count of ones in a word is always even or always odd
the number of distinct states that a counting circuit passes through
items.s: NAND gate: a device whose output is low only when every input is high. The other options describe Open collector output, Parity bit, Modulus.

items.q: Which term is described by “an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus”?
o: Tri state output
Fan out
Transistor transistor logic
Power dissipation
items.s: Tri state output is an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Half adder.
o: a signed notation in which a negative number is the inverse of its magnitude plus one
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
a circuit that forms the sum and carry of two single bits
a two state storage element that changes only at a defined edge of a clock
items.s: Half adder: a circuit that forms the sum and carry of two single bits. The other options describe De Morgan law, Two’s complement, Flip flop.

items.q: Which of the following best describes De Morgan law?
o: a shift register that feeds back the inverse of its last stage
a fault in which the result depends on which of two nearly simultaneous changes arrives first
a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
items.s: De Morgan law: the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions. The other options describe Shift register, Johnson counter, Race condition.

items.q: The statement “a device whose output is high only when every input is low” describes which of the following?
o: Truth table
NAND gate
NOR gate
Universal gate
items.s: NOR gate is a device whose output is high only when every input is low.

items.q: A binary decoder is given 5 input lines. How many output lines does it have?
items.s: One output is active for each input code, so 2^5 = 32 outputs.

items.q: The 12 bit two's complement word 100001110111 is to be read as a signed number. What decimal value does it represent?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative. Its value is 2167 minus 2^12 = -1929.

items.q: A binary counter is built from 7 flip flops. What is its natural modulus?
items.s: The counter runs through 2^7 = 128 states before repeating.

items.q: A 8 bit word is to be shifted out of a shift register one place per clock. How many clock pulses are needed to clear the whole word?
items.s: Each of the 8 bits needs one clock pulse, so 8 pulses empty the register.

items.q: A memory is organised as 2048 words of 8 bits. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 2048 x 8 = 16384 bits.

items.q: A logic family guarantees a minimum output high of 2.4 V and requires at least 1.8 V at its inputs. What is the high level noise margin in volts?
items.s: Noise margin = output high minus input high = 2.4 - 1.8 = 0.6 V.

items.q: The integer 99 is shifted left by 2 places inside a register that is wide enough to hold the result. What value does the register then hold?
items.s: A left shift of 2 multiplies by 2^2, so 99 x 4 = 396.

items.q: Convert the binary number 10011 to decimal.
items.s: Adding the place values 1, 2, 4, 8 ... where a one appears in 10011 gives 19.

items.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 6B to decimal.
items.s: Each hexadecimal place is a power of sixteen, and 6B works out to 107.

items.q: A register stores 16 bits. How many hexadecimal digits are needed to write its whole content?
items.s: One hex digit covers four bits, so 16 bits need 16/4 = 4 digits.

items.q: How many binary places are required to express the decimal number 1398?
items.s: The largest power of two below 1398 is 2^10, so 11 bits are needed.

items.q: A nibble of a register holds the hexadecimal digit 8. What decimal value does that nibble stand for?
items.s: The hex digit 8 has place value 8 in decimal.

items.q: A multiplexer is controlled by 5 select lines. How many data inputs can it choose between?
items.s: Each select line doubles the choices, so 2^5 = 32 inputs.

items.q: A ripple carry adder is built from half adders for the first stage and full adders afterwards to add two 7 bit words. How many adder blocks are needed in all?
items.s: One block serves each of the 7 columns: a half adder for the first column and a full adder for each of the remaining 6 columns, giving 7 blocks in all.

items.q: A signed integer is stored in two's complement in 10 bits. What is the magnitude of the most negative value it can hold?
items.s: The most negative value is -2^9, whose magnitude is 512.

items.q: A combinational path passes through 6 gate levels and each gate delays by 20 ns. What is the worst case path delay?
items.s: Delays in series add, so 6 x 20 = 120 ns.

items.q: A counting circuit must pass through 5 distinct states. What is the smallest number of flip flops that will serve?
items.s: k stages give 2^k states, so the least k with 2^k at least 5 is 3.

items.q: A ripple counter has 3 stages and each flip flop has a propagation delay of 20 ns. What is the total delay before the output settles after a clock?
items.s: The delays of the 3 stages add up, so 3 x 20 = 60 ns.

items.q: A ring counter is built from 4 flip flops. How many distinct states does it pass through?
items.s: A single one circulates through the 4 stages, so the counter has 4 states.

items.q: A Johnson counter is built from 8 flip flops. How many distinct states does it pass through?
items.s: Inverting feedback doubles the number of stages, so the counter has 2 x 8 = 16 states.

items.q: A store of 8192 words is to be built from chips each holding 1024 words. How many chips are required?
A read only memory is used to store a function of 5 inputs, one word per input pattern. How many words must the memory hold?
items.s: Each of the 2^5 = 32 input patterns needs its own word.

items.q: A gate can sink 24 mA at its output, and every input it drives sinks 1 mA when low. What is the fan out allowed by current sinking?
items.s: Fan out = sink capability divided by current per input = 24/1 = 24 inputs.

items.q: A synchronous circuit has a critical path of 25 ns between registers. What is the highest clock frequency it can use, in MHz?
items.s: Frequency = 1/period = 1/25 ns = 40 MHz.

items.q: A gate has a propagation delay of 15 ns and dissipates 2 mW. What is its delay power product in picojoules?
items.s: Delay power product = 15 ns x 2 mW = 30 pJ.

items.q: An 8 bit digital to analogue converter has a full scale output of 5 V. What output results from the input code 216?
items.s: Output = full scale x code/2^bits = 5 x 216/256 = 4.22 V.

items.q: An 8 bit word holds the value 157. How many of its bits are set to one?
items.s: 157 in binary is 10011101, which has 5 ones.

items.q: Two 8 bit words 10101101 and 10110000 are combined with a bitwise AND. What decimal value results?
items.s: A bit is one only where both words have a one, and that pattern is worth 160.

items.q: Two 8 bit words 103 and 144 are combined with a bitwise OR. What decimal value results?
items.s: Bringing together the set bits of both words gives 247.

items.q: Two 8 bit words 117 and 87 are combined with an exclusive OR. What decimal value results?
items.s: Only the positions where the words differ survive, and they are worth 34.

items.q: A seven segment display shows the decimal digit 5. How many of its segments are lit?
items.s: The digit 5 needs 5 of the seven segments.

items.q: How many cells must a Karnaugh map have if it is to represent a function of 2 variables?
items.s: One cell per minterm gives 2^2 = 4 cells.

items.q: A binary decoder is given 2 input lines. How many output lines does it have?
items.s: One output is active for each input code, so 2^2 = 4 outputs.

items.q: The 16 bit two's complement word 1100011111100010 is to be read as a signed number. What decimal value does it represent?
items.s: The leading bit is one, so the word is negative. Its value is 51170 minus 2^16 = -14366.

items.q: A binary counter is built from 5 flip flops. What is its natural modulus?
items.s: The counter runs through 2^5 = 32 states before repeating.

items.q: A 16 bit word is to be shifted out of a shift register one place per clock. How many clock pulses are needed to clear the whole word?
items.s: Each of the 16 bits needs one clock pulse, so 16 pulses empty the register.

items.q: A memory is organised as 512 words of 8 bits. What is its capacity in bits?
items.s: Capacity = words x bits per word = 512 x 8 = 4096 bits.

items.q: A logic family guarantees a minimum output high of 3.5 V and requires at least 2.2 V at its inputs. What is the high level noise margin in volts?
items.s: Noise margin = output high minus input high = 3.5 - 2.2 = 1.3 V.

items.q: An integrated circuit contains 50 gates, each dissipating 2 mW. What is the total dissipation in milliwatts?
items.s: Total = 50 x 2 = 100 mW.

items.q: A 8 bit analogue to digital converter has a full scale range of 10 V. What is its resolution in volts?
items.s: Resolution = full scale / 2^bits = 10/256 = 0.0391 V.

items.q: The integer 39 is shifted left by 1 places inside a register that is wide enough to hold the result. What value does the register then hold?
items.s: A left shift of 1 multiplies by 2^1, so 39 x 2 = 78.

items.q: Convert the binary number 111011101 to decimal.
items.s: Adding the place values 1, 2, 4, 8 ... where a one appears in 111011101 gives 477.

items.q: Convert the hexadecimal number A87 to decimal.
items.s: Each hexadecimal place is a power of sixteen, and A87 works out to 2695.

items.q: A register stores 12 bits. How many hexadecimal digits are needed to write its whole content?
items.s: One hex digit covers four bits, so 12 bits need 12/4 = 3 digits.

items.q: How many binary places are required to express the decimal number 3414?
items.s: The largest power of two below 3414 is 2^11, so 12 bits are needed.

items.q: A nibble of a register holds the hexadecimal digit D. What decimal value does that nibble stand for?
items.s: The hex digit D has place value 13 in decimal.

items.q: A complete truth table is required for a circuit with 4 inputs. How many rows must it contain?
items.s: Every input doubles the rows, so 2^4 = 16 rows.

items.q: A group of 2 adjacent cells is circled on a Karnaugh map. How many variables are eliminated from the corresponding term?
items.s: Grouping 2 = 2^1 cells removes 1 variables from the term.

items.q: A ripple carry adder is built from half adders for the first stage and full adders afterwards to add two 5 bit words. How many adder blocks are needed in all?
items.s: One block serves each of the 5 columns: a half adder for the first column and a full adder for each of the remaining 4 columns, giving 5 blocks in all.

items.q: A half adder has 4 inputs listed in its full truth table including the carry in for comparison. How many rows does that table have?
items.s: With 4 inputs the table needs 2^4 = 16 rows.

items.q: A signed integer is stored in two's complement in 32 bits. What is the magnitude of the most negative value it can hold?
items.s: The most negative value is -2^31, whose magnitude is 2147483648.

items.q: A ripple counter has 8 stages and each flip flop has a propagation delay of 25 ns. What is the total delay before the output settles after a clock?
items.s: The delays of the 8 stages add up, so 8 x 25 = 200 ns.

items.q: A ring counter is built from 8 flip flops. How many distinct states does it pass through?
items.s: A single one circulates through the 8 stages, so the counter has 8 states.

items.q: A Johnson counter is built from 5 flip flops. How many distinct states does it pass through?
items.s: Inverting feedback doubles the number of stages, so the counter has 2 x 5 = 10 states.

items.q: A memory contains 1024 addressable words. How many address lines must the chip be given?
items.s: The address must count up to 1024, so k address lines give 2^k words and 2^10 = 1024.

items.q: A read only memory is used to store a function of 2 inputs, one word per input pattern. How many words must the memory hold?
items.s: Each of the 2^2 = 4 input patterns needs its own word.

items.q: A gate can sink 24 mA at its output, and every input it drives sinks 1.6 mA when low. What is the fan out allowed by current sinking?
items.s: Fan out = sink capability divided by current per input = 24/1.6 = 15 inputs.

items.q: A synchronous circuit has a critical path of 15 ns between registers. What is the highest clock frequency it can use, in MHz?
items.s: Frequency = 1/period = 1/15 ns = 66.67 MHz.

items.q: A gate has a propagation delay of 10 ns and dissipates 2 mW. What is its delay power product in picojoules?
items.s: Delay power product = 10 ns x 2 mW = 20 pJ.

items.q: An 5 bit digital to analogue converter has a full scale output of 15 V. What output results from the input code 21?
items.s: Output = full scale x code/2^bits = 15 x 21/32 = 9.84 V.

items.q: The statement “a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input” describes which of the following?
o: Clock skew
State table
Metastability
Latch
items.s: State table is a listing of the next state and output of a circuit for each present state and input.

items.q: The statement “the difference between the true value and the nearest step a converter can represent” describes which of the following?
o: Analogue to digital converter
Resolution of a converter
Quantisation error
Sample and hold
items.s: Quantisation error is the difference between the true value and the nearest step a converter can represent.

the condition in which a result is too large for the number of places available
a circuit that turns a measured voltage into a binary word
a circuit that freezes a changing voltage while it is being converted
items.s: Analogue to digital converter: a circuit that turns a measured voltage into a binary word. The other options describe Overflow, Full scale range, Sample and hold.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rightmost digit of a binary word, which carries the smallest weight”?
o: Bit position weight
Parity bit
Least significant bit
Octal digit

items.q: In this course, Absorption rule refers to

the rule that a term implied by two others may be deleted without changing a function
the identity by which a term swallows any larger term that contains it
an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Quantisation error means.
o: a circuit that freezes a changing voltage while it is being converted
the condition in which a result is too large for the number of places available
the difference between the true value and the nearest step a converter can represent
the span of input from zero to the largest value a converter can represent
items.s: Quantisation error: the difference between the true value and the nearest step a converter can represent. The other options describe Full scale range, Overflow, Sample and hold.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Logic swing means.
o: an output that can pull low but needs an external resistor to pull high
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
the difference between the high and the low output levels of a gate
a family built from bipolar transistors in which inputs are emitters
items.s: Logic swing: the difference between the high and the low output levels of a gate. The other options describe Transistor transistor logic, Propagation delay product, Open collector output.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the smallest change of input that a converter can distinguish”
o: Analogue to digital converter
Sample and hold
Digital to analogue converter
Resolution of a converter

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the number of distinct states that a counting circuit passes through”
o: Johnson counter
Modulus
Counter
Synchronous counter
items.s: Modulus is the number of distinct states that a counting circuit passes through.

items.q: In this course, Register refers to
o: a shift register whose last stage feeds the first so that a single one circulates
a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it
a reset input that acts at once without waiting for a clock edge
a group of storage elements that hold one binary word
items.s: Register: a group of storage elements that hold one binary word. The other options describe Asynchronous clear, Ring counter, Ripple counter.

items.q: The best definition of Karnaugh map among these is
o: a rectangular arrangement of cells in Gray order used to group minterms by eye
a sum of every variable of a function that is false for exactly one input pattern
the rule that a term implied by two others may be deleted without changing a function
an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs
items.s: Karnaugh map: a rectangular arrangement of cells in Gray order used to group minterms by eye. The other options describe Maxterm, Consensus theorem, Don’t care condition.

items.q: Which term is described by “a reset input that acts at once without waiting for a clock edge”?
o: Synchronous counter
Ripple counter
Asynchronous clear
Modulus
items.s: Asynchronous clear is a reset input that acts at once without waiting for a clock edge.

items.q: The best definition of Boolean variable among these is
o: one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted
a quantity that can hold only the value true or the value false
an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs
the rule that inverting a product gives a sum of inversions and inverting a sum gives a product of inversions
items.s: Boolean variable: a quantity that can hold only the value true or the value false. The other options describe Don’t care condition, Literal, De Morgan law.

items.q: The best definition of Ripple counter among these is

a shift register whose last stage feeds the first so that a single one circulates
a shift register that feeds back the inverse of its last stage
a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it
items.s: Ripple counter: a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it. The other options describe Ring counter, Johnson counter, Presettable counter.

items.q: In this course, Parity bit refers to
o: an extra bit added so that the count of ones in a word is always even or always odd
a symbol from zero to nine or A to F standing for four binary places
the power of the base attached to each place in a positional numeral
the leftmost digit of a binary word, which carries the greatest weight
items.s: Parity bit: an extra bit added so that the count of ones in a word is always even or always odd. The other options describe Most significant bit, Hexadecimal digit, Bit position weight.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Propagation delay product means.
o: the energy a gate converts to heat in each second of operation
a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off
an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
items.s: Propagation delay product: the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation. The other options describe Tri state output, CMOS inverter, Power dissipation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an expression formed by adding together the minterms where the output is true”
o: Boolean variable
Canonical sum
Literal
Karnaugh map
items.s: Canonical sum is an expression formed by adding together the minterms where the output is true.

items.q: The best definition of Most significant bit among these is
o: a symbol that takes only the value zero or one in base two
the leftmost digit of a binary word, which carries the greatest weight
the coding of each decimal digit separately as four binary places
an ordering of binary words in which neighbours differ in exactly one place
items.s: Most significant bit: the leftmost digit of a binary word, which carries the greatest weight. The other options describe Binary digit, Gray code, Binary coded decimal.

items.q: CMOS inverter is best described as
o: an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus
a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off
the number of inputs that one output can drive while keeping its levels valid
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
items.s: CMOS inverter: a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off. The other options describe Propagation delay product, Tri state output, Fan out.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an ordering of binary words in which neighbours differ in exactly one place”
o: Least significant bit
Octal digit
Gray code
Most significant bit

items.q: Which term is described by “one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted”?
o: Literal
Absorption rule
Karnaugh map
Maxterm
items.s: Literal is one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted.

items.q: In this course, Gray code refers to
o: the leftmost digit of a binary word, which carries the greatest weight
the rightmost digit of a binary word, which carries the smallest weight
the coding of each decimal digit separately as four binary places
an ordering of binary words in which neighbours differ in exactly one place
items.s: Gray code: an ordering of binary words in which neighbours differ in exactly one place. The other options describe Least significant bit, Binary coded decimal, Most significant bit.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the delay from presenting an address to receiving the word stored there”
o: Volatile store
Access time
Programmable array logic
Flash memory

items.q: In this course, Logic swing refers to
o: a pair of complementary transistors in which one is always off
the difference between the high and the low output levels of a gate
the energy a gate consumes for each switching operation, found by multiplying delay by dissipation
an output that can be high, low or disconnected from the bus
items.s: Logic swing: the difference between the high and the low output levels of a gate. The other options describe Tri state output, Propagation delay product, CMOS inverter.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a conductor carrying one bit of the number that selects a stored word”
o: Address line
Word line
Read only memory
Volatile store
items.s: Address line is a conductor carrying one bit of the number that selects a stored word.

items.q: The statement “a chain of storage elements that passes its content one place per clock” describes which of the following?
o: Ripple counter
Presettable counter
Ring counter
Shift register

items.q: The statement “a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs” describes which of the following?
o: NOR gate
Combinational circuit
Half adder
Truth table
items.s: Truth table is a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Sum of products form means.
o: an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition
a circuit that forms the sum and carry of two single bits
a circuit that adds two bits together with a carry arriving from a lower place
a listing of the output of a circuit for every possible combination of its inputs
items.s: Sum of products form: an arrangement of a function as product terms joined by addition. The other options describe Full adder, Truth table, Half adder.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs”
o: Boolean variable
Don’t care condition
Consensus theorem
Literal
items.s: Don’t care condition is an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs.

items.q: Literal is best described as

the rule that a term implied by two others may be deleted without changing a function
one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted
an input pattern for which the output may be either value because it never occurs
items.s: Literal: one appearance of a variable either as it stands or inverted. The other options describe Consensus theorem, Canonical sum, Don’t care condition.

items.q: The best definition of Synchronous counter among these is

a counting circuit in which every stage receives the same clock at the same instant
the number of distinct states that a counting circuit passes through
a counting chain in which each stage is clocked by the output of the stage before it

an array in which any word can be read or written in the same access time
a memory whose content is lost when the supply is removed

Register
Asynchronous clear
Synchronous counter

Word line

Logic swing

items.q: A logic family guarantees a minimum output high of 3.5 V and requires at least 1.8 V at its inputs. What is the high level noise margin in volts?
items.s: Noise margin = output high minus input high = 3.5 - 1.8 = 1.7 V.

items.q: An 4 bit digital to analogue converter has a full scale output of 10 V. What output results from the input code 1?
items.s: Output = full scale x code/2^bits = 10 x 1/16 = 0.625 V.

items.q: An 8 bit word holds the value 488. How many of its bits are set to one?
items.s: 488 in binary is 111101000, which has 5 ones.
